Why is the (111) plane in an FCC crystal more densely packed than the (111) plane in a BCC crystal of the same atomic radius?
set.c.W: The FCC (111) plane contains contributions from three corner atoms and three face-centered atoms, while the BCC (111) plane contains only contributions from the three corner atoms
set.c.X: The (111) plane in BCC has a larger geometric area than the (111) plane in FCC, which reduces its areal atom count
set.c.Y: FCC has a smaller lattice parameter than BCC for the same atomic radius, so all FCC planes are denser than all BCC planes
set.c.Z: The body-centered atom in BCC repels atoms in the (111) plane outward, lowering the planar density
set.a.t: The FCC (111) plane contains contributions from three corner atoms and three face-centered atoms, while the BCC (111) plane contains only contributions from the three corner atoms
